To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T(3) activates the MCL- 1 gene promoter in a non-genomic manner, using the PI3-kinase signal transduction pathway.
thyroid hormone activates MCL-1 transcription by a non-genomical, non-retinoid X receptor, PI3-K-dependent mechanism.
triiodothyronine increases the expression of anti-apoptotic protein myeloid cell-leukemia-1 via a non-genomic, cAMP-dependent mechanism that involves phosphatidylinositide 3-kinases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which thyroid hormone regulates apoptosis in cells of different developmental stages, cell type, or pathophysiological state.
the molecular mechanisms of thyroid hormone regulation of MCL-1 gene expression in human cells,
the molecular mechanisms leading from T(3) binding to its receptor to MCL-1 activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T(3) utilizes the PI3-K pathway to activate the MCL- 1 promoter and, consequently, to increase the MCL- protein expression in thyroid hormone receptor- expressing HK2 cells.
T(3) utilizes PI3-K signal pathway to activate MCL-1, which is an important anti-apoptotic protein.
thyroid hormone receptor beta-1, when bound to triiodothyronine, increases the transcription from MCL-1 gene promoter by a non-genome mechanism using the phosphatidylinositole 3-kinases pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T(3) induces MCL-1 gene expression by a non-genomically regulated mechanism using the PI 3-kinse pathway.
thyroid hormones regulate the expression of the MCL1 gene via the cAMP-responsive element and the PI3K signal transduction pathway.
T(3) utilizes PI3-K pathway to increase MCL-1 protein expression, which in turn protects cells from apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thyroid hormone receptor beta is a transcriptional activator of the anti-apoptotic MCL-1 gene.
thyroid hormone receptor beta-1, in cooperation with cAMP-responsive element binding protein and PI3-K, increases MCL-1 transcription, which leads to the anti-apoptotic effect of T3.
